headline: Western Oregon overtake Seattle Pacific to finish top
dek: Western Oregon won at Western Washington on Saturday and finish the conference season above Seattle Pacific, whose own schedule had already ended with a win over Northwest Nazarene. Western Oregon's only defeat by a member came at Seattle Pacific in October.
displaced_by: Western Oregon won at Western Washington and finish above Seattle Pacific, so the standing lines about Seattle Pacific waiting on Saturday's result are no longer true.

pattern.label: derived
pattern.text: Saint Martin's 32 goals are more than Simon Fraser, Western Washington or Northwest Nazarene have scored, yet they sit bottom of the table: most of their goals have come against sides outside the conference, not in the matches the table counts.

wire.line: Western Oregon finish top, having won every match since their goalless draw at Northwest Nazarene.

findings.label: observed
findings.text: Three matches whose dates have passed carry no result, and every one of them is a Simon Fraser home match from August.

findings.label: derived
findings.text: Seattle Pacific have won fifteen matches, more than any other programme in the conference.

findings.label: observed
findings.text: Archie Dhima has 16 goals from 53 shots for Western Oregon.

findings.label: observed
findings.text: Elijah Brockl has kept seven shutouts for Northwest Nazarene.

findings.label: observed
findings.text: Of the shots on target Austin Valdez has faced for Western Oregon, 83 were saved and 22 went in.

last_match.line: Western Washington have now lost to Western Oregon home and away.

next_match.line: Simon Fraser have not beaten Seattle Pacific in either meeting this season.

validation.policy: observed and derived claims are recomputed against the data home before publish; failures are dropped, not softened. signal and projected pass on schema unless the data contradicts a figure. context is never validated as a finding.
